does: Leaves washed rice in cold water until the grains have turned white and plump all through, so that they cook evenly and come out tender in the middle.

intro.what: This rice method soaks washed grains in cold water before draining and cooking in fresh measured water.
intro.why: It teaches you to recognise hydration and keep soaking separate from final cooking-liquid control.

how: Put the washed, drained rice in the pot or in a bowl and cover it with cold water.
Leave it until the grains turn from clear to chalky white.
Drain it well and let it sit in the sieve for a short while.
Cook it in fresh measured water.

cues.text: The grains turn from glassy to an even, chalky white.
A grain crushes easily between the fingers, with no hard core.

mistakes.mistake: Soaking for too long in warm weather, so that the rice sours.
mistakes.fix: Soak it in cold water and shorter.

mistakes.mistake: Cooking it in the soaking water, so that the amount of water is wrong.
mistakes.fix: Drain it and add the measured water.

quiz.question: Why soak the washed rice in this method?
choices: To dry out the grain centres.
To remove the need for cooking liquid.
To hydrate the centres for more even softening.
quiz.because: Absorbed water reaches into the grains before cooking begins.

quiz.question: What happens after the rice has soaked?
choices: Drain it and cook in fresh measured water.
Keep adding unmeasured water to the soaking bowl.
Cook it with whatever soaking water remains.
quiz.because: Separating the soak from cooking allows the cooking water to be controlled deliberately.

quiz.question: Which colour change shows hydration here?
choices: Only the outside looks white while a glassy centre remains.
Glassy grains turn evenly chalky white.
Only dry white tips appear on transparent centres.
quiz.because: These grains turn evenly chalky white as water reaches their interiors.

quiz.question: The final water amount is inconsistent after soaking. What should change?
choices: Leave the soaking liquid and top it up by eye.
Add extra water every time without draining.
Drain the soaking water before adding measured cooking water.
quiz.because: Removing variable leftover soaking water makes the next addition more consistent.

comes_after.why: The rice is soaked after it has been washed.

variant_of.differs: It is a short soak of washed rice in cold water until the grains turn white, and not a long soak of dried pulses, and the water is poured off.
